lead: CVE-2025-6514, command injection in mcp-remote, JFrog, July 2025
note: A critical remote code execution flaw in a widely installed MCP client, found by researchers and fixed in 0.1.16. No exploitation of a named organisation is on the record, so there is no harm to trace to a missing control. A vulnerability with no incident is what the register calls a hazard, and hazards are only admitted when the organisation confirms a near miss.

lead: CVE-2025-59536, Claude Code SessionStart hook runs before the trust prompt, Check Point, 2026
note: A malicious repository could run commands before Claude Code showed its trust dialog. Disclosed by researchers and fixed. No named organisation reports harm from it.

lead: CVE-2026-22708, Cursor allowlist bypass through shell built-ins, Pillar Security, 2026
note: Shell built-ins such as export ran in Auto-Run allowlist mode without approval, which let injected content poison the environment of commands the user had approved. Fixed in Cursor 2.3. Researcher disclosure with no reported harm to a named organisation.

lead: Mini Shai-Hulud npm worm, persistence through .claude/settings.json, May 2026
note: The closest call so far. The worm compromised packages belonging to TanStack, Mistral AI, Guardrails AI, UiPath and others, and it wrote a SessionStart hook into Claude Code's settings file so the stealer re-ran whenever a developer opened the project. That makes an agent's config file an autostart location, which is the role a shell profile plays, and it spread through package installs rather than through anything the agent chose to do. No agent call, send or data change is in the record, so the harm does not trace to an agent control. Worth revisiting if a version is documented where the agent itself carried the action.
